storyBeats.detail: The creator reaches the Kailasagiri/Kailasagiri-area approach and starts explaining the small route toward the hill and temple area.

The creator contrasts the area with an earlier visit several years ago, noting that it is now much more crowded/traffic-heavy. This is a useful lived observation and supports the sense that the place has become more popular.
The creator points out that the temple is inside the hill and explains the path in front, turning the visual destination into something the viewer can understand before the exploration.

The creator explains that the route continues upward on foot and reacts to the amount of walking, including fatigue and leg discomfort. This adds authentic physical experience rather than generic destination narration.

There are destination-area interactions/questions and observations around nearby organizations, signs/locations and people. Several ASR segments are low-confidence, so dialogue should be listen-checked before making it a major story beat.
The creator comments on a sudden change in heat and later notices posters/hoardings and local surroundings. These are texture beats rather than core plot points.

A clear line at 01:08.690–01:11.810 says the creator will show an aerial view using the selfie stick. This can become a visual payoff only if the corresponding footage actually shows the intended overview.

Later bundle-002 material appears to continue the destination exploration before the major off-road payoff preserved in bundle 004. Use bundle 002 to establish place and human atmosphere, not to duplicate later adventure footage.

finalMergeGuidance: Bundle 002 should provide the destination middle of the vlog: the viewer understands that the area has become busy, sees/understands the hill-and-temple concept, and feels the creator physically beginning the climb. Keep the storytelling conversational and observational. Use short music/visual breaths where they add atmosphere, but avoid long generic destination narration.
